prompts.text: What's a tiny decision you spend longer thinking about than it deserves?
A person who offers two clear options makes choosing somewhere to go much easier.
We're choosing between two concerts on the same evening. What detail would help you decide?
Choosing the route with the best scenery or the route which gets you there ten minutes sooner?
Tell me about a small decision you made on impulse which turned into a favourite memory.
Some people read every menu before arriving, while others decide only when the waiter appears.
When you face two equally appealing options, what usually breaks the tie?
There is something reassuring about admitting you don't mind which option wins.
We each have one free hour and four possible things to do. How would you narrow the list?
Taking turns choosing the activity or finding a third option neither of us suggested?
